Fundamental Ethereum White Paper Coming Next Week

A fundamental White Paper by Charles Holloway that promises to shake up the Ethereum community will be published next week. The White Paper is being released, at no cost, just in time to be a major topic of discussion at the upcoming Ethereum Developer’s Conference in London, Nov 9 through 13. (https://devcon.ethereum.org/))

Ethereum is a blockchain-based technology, similar to Bitcoin, that enables individuals, businesses and even entire industries to be decentralized, net-distributed, and completely privately operated. The Ethereum Development community’s (ETHDEV) slogan is “How the Internet was supposed to work.”

Proponents of Ethereum claim the technology is innovative, disruptive to traditional internet business models, and because activities are encrypted, not subject to political inefficiencies. There is an emerging rush to develop the technology similar to the rush to develop the World Wide Web during the mid-1990's. Many anticipate that Ethereum is the space from which the next generation of Internet billionaires will emerge.

Ethereum developers are building a technology called “smart contracts,” that many anticipate will change the way Internet commerce is done. And now, according to Holloway’s upcoming paper, the additional revolutionary concept of Open Source Government, when combined with smart contract technology, amounts to nothing less than a complete redesign of human civilization.

The paper’s author, Charles Holloway, is a writer and futurist who lives in Southern California. “I’m not even a coder,” Holloway says. “It’s only my interest in scientific epistemology that’s enabled me to do something so relevant to the Ethereum community, and so fundamental.”

There’s nothing light-weight about Holloway’s upcoming paper. It’s reportedly about 70,000 words long, the length of a short book. “I know it seems long, but it’s impossible to impart the information necessary to understand this technology in anything less,” Holloway says.

Holloway’s paper is a sweeping historical/scientific treatise that tackles some of the most vexing topics in human history with astonishing clarity, matter-of-fact thinking, and scientifically precise semantics. It is for serious scientific thinkers who realize that humanity is on the cusp of major changes, and it points the way for the unlimited positive (and financial) potential of Ethereum.

Open Source Government; The Foundational Concepts will be published on Holloway’s website (chasholloway.com) and will be announced on the Ethereum forum sometime during the week of October 26, 2015. It will be free of charge to download. Everyone with a stake in the future is invited to read it and join in the “OSG” revolution.

For more info, contact:

Bill Hergonson at hergonosg@gmail.com Chas Holloway at chasosg@gmail.com

Chas, any chance you could give us a couple of examples of how a smart contract would work from a layman's perspective, and how it would relate to open source governance?

A written contract contains fundamental two things: operational terms (for ex, when condition A happens, take action B -- pay money, collect money, etc.) and logical terms (how the operations logically fit together). English language (or French, German, Spanish, etc) are terrible at containing logical and operational terms non-ambiguously. A much better language would be computer code. You can get all the ambiguity out. And that eliminates 99% of the need for arbitration.

A smart contract is written in code. It lives on a blockchain based platform like Ethereum so it's distributed (no central location; it exists everywhere), it's encrypted (that means it's totally private and invisible to the State or to criminals), and it contains automated processes -- it's like a little bot that can run all over the net and do stuff for you. Currently smart contracts are being used to do rudimentary things like connection protocols. But the technology is developing to do all sorts of things. Eventually they'll replace paper contracts. The OSG white paper is about how you can use this technology (and a few other technologies) a much freer society than can ever exist under a political state.

Well, the technology is being developed. But it's not the only technology -- smart contracts will be operating in conjunction with other technologies that are also being developed. Went to lunch and felt guilty for not giving you an adequate answer. It could work something like this: let's say you (A) bet (B) on who will win a football game. A smart contract could act as an agent between the both of you. At a designated time (an hour after the game ends) the smart contract, itself, would access a database somewhere that has the final score. Once it has that data, it would then automatically deposit the winnings into the winner's wallet.

So in this case, you would need 1) a smart contract that contains specified operations when certain conditions are met, and 2) a database containing the info the smart contract needs to check the current state of conditions. Once you (Mr. A and Mr. B) launch the contract, everything happens automatically.

Add to this: the contract lives on a blockchain-based platform. When the contract has completed, it self-destructs, goes out of existence (although the company that provides the contract may be there to offer you its services, again). It's also encrypted, so all activities are totally invisible to anyone but A and B.
